_about: Glossary of period words (press G in the game). Checked against the Dictionary of South African English (dsae.co.za) where noted in research.md section 21.
glossary.title: Words of the road
glossary.footer: Up/down to scroll. Any other key to close.
glossary.laager.text: A camp with the wagons drawn into a ring, often lashed together, to protect people and animals at night or in danger.
glossary.voorloper.text: The person who walks in front of the oxen, leading the front pair by a thong and picking the way. Often a boy or a Khoikhoi servant.
glossary.smous.text: A travelling trader who took goods to farms far from any town, often taking sheep in payment.
glossary.drift.text: A ford: a place where a river is shallow enough to cross.
glossary.kakebeenwa.text: The trek wagon, named 'jawbone wagon' for the shape of its sides.
glossary.span.text: A team of oxen pulling one wagon, usually twelve to sixteen.
glossary.inspan.text: To yoke the oxen to the wagon, and to unyoke them for a rest. An outspan is also a resting place.
glossary.disselboom.text: The long wooden pole of the wagon, to which the yokes of the oxen are fixed.
glossary.juk.text: The wooden yoke across a pair of oxen's necks, and the wooden pins that hold it in place.
glossary.sanna.text: Names for the trekkers' long muzzle-loading guns. A sterloop had a star marked near the muzzle.
glossary.muid.text: A measure for grain and meal; a muid of meal weighed about 180 lb.
glossary.rixdollar.text: The old Cape money, still used by many people in 1837. From 1825 one rixdollar was worth one shilling and sixpence, so a pound was about 13 rixdollars.
glossary.groot_rivier.text: 'Great River': the trekkers' name for the Orange River.
glossary.spoor.text: The tracks or trail of an animal or person.
glossary.kraal.text: An enclosure for cattle or sheep; also a village or homestead.
glossary.karos.text: A cloak or blanket made of animal skins sewn together.
glossary.biltong.text: Meat cut into strips, salted and dried in the wind. It keeps for months.
glossary.beskuit.text: Rusks: bread baked a second time until hard and dry, so it keeps on a long journey.
glossary.field_cornet.text: A local official in a farming district of the Colony.
glossary.trekboer.text: A farmer who moved about with his herds in search of grazing, as many Dutch frontier families had done since the 1700s.
